QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_20

question.text: Under SAS-200 the Ophthalmology CSR cataract programme reports 85% improvement in vision outcomes. The SIA's sub-sample re-interview finds only 68% of re-contacted beneficiaries confirm sustained vision improvement 6 months post-surgery. The MOST appropriate disclosure is:

answer.text: Report the 85% figure as provided by the SE with no adjustment
Report both figures with the sub-sample methodology, flag the variance as a reliability concern in Section III Limitations and discuss whether the gap is material enough to modify the conclusion
Report the 68% sub-sample figure only and ignore the SE number
Take an average (76.5%) and report that

explanation.text: **The Logic:** The SIA must disclose both numbers transparently — the SE's reported figure and the independent sub-sample reperformance figure — and let the user of the report understand the variance. Averaging hides evidence, hiding either number is misleading. **The Trap:** Option A ignores SIA independent evidence. Option C ignores the SE's fuller data. Option D manufactures a figure with no methodological basis. **Cross-Exam Context:** Reliability-variance disclosure matches III-C (Compliance — internal-audit exceptions) and XV (Research Analyst — survey response-quality disclosure). **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Pre-declare in the engagement letter that sub-sample re-interview results will be reported alongside SE figures. This pre-empts SE management pushback at Report drafting stage.
